Does anyone here have/use an Air Fryer? I got one for Xmas and I'm looking for tips.

So far my experience has been decidedly mediocre. My wife has celiacs so we eat a lot of gluten free stuff. We tried making some GF chicken nuggets (Perdue) and they were a little dry. I think we left them in too long. They did get cripsy. 

Last night we tried making artichoke hearts and carrots (from frozen bags) and they cooked fine but didn't get crispy or anything. We use the highest setting (390) on the fryer. 

Anyone have one of these and know some tricks or tips? Thanks.

Roommate mixed arborio and sushi rice together. Need help!

The mix is probably 60% arborio and 40% sushi. I always thought they had vastly different uses, but I could be wrong. Is there a recipe that could benefit from both kinds? How interchangeable are these? Please let me know your thoughts.

What are some uses for this? I'll throw some into baked beans, and I know cracklin is an option, but what else can I do with the flesh besides give it to the neighbor's dog?

I like making those breakfast egg cups in with the muffin tin but I'd like a little bit of breading in it every now and then. What happens if I add a little piece of dough in with the mixed veggies/cheese and then pour the eggs over it all?

How would I make chicken breaded with Takis?

Hello folks,  
Let me just start by saying I absolutely love fuego Takis! I think they would go really well as breading for chicken due to their flavor, spice level and crunch. I’ve tried to bake them in the oven, and they actually come out with a good level of crispiness, but the breading doesn’t retain any of the taki flavor or spiciness. How can I make this while still keeping the same flavor?  
  
My recipe was small pieces of chicken dipped in flour, egg wash, then crushed takis. I poured 1/2 cup of olive oil onto the chicken and then baked them in a toaster oven at 350*F for 30 mins and then flipped and baked again for 20 mins. Can anyone suggest a better recipe?

Does anyone else ever completely lose interest in cooking/food?

I'm typically the type of person who loves to cook at home. When I'm not in the kitchen I spend my free time hunting for recipes, watching YouTube cooking videos, and reading food blogs and cook books. But for whatever reason, over the last month or two this has completely changed. Cooking and eating is now a chore. I've completely lost interest in all things food-related and can't be bothered to turn on the stove. Food has become a source of frustration and annoyance; it pisses me off that I need to eat 3+ times a day in order to survive. It's so damn inconvenient. I know this is becoming bad for my health because I'm mostly eating cereal, convenience food, and takeout. Because I'm the primary cook in my house, it's affecting my husband whose eating habits have also become horribly unhealthy as a result.  


Has anyone else experienced this? How did you get back into cooking when it's the last thing you feel like doing? I really want to snap out of this funk.

Anyone else have a problem with using way too many paper towels while cooking, or is it just me?

Open a packet of something and get a little schmutz on your fingers? Paper towel. Have to wipe down a pan or plate quick? Paper towel. Spill a little something on the counter or the floor? Paper towel. Need to pat the moisture off of meat? Paper towel. Washing my hands after handling raw meat? Paper towel. Frying something and need to get the oil off as quickly as possible? Paper towel. Finally ready to eat and don't have napkins? Paper towel.

I never really notice how much I use until I look at the garbage and see the mounds of paper towels filling up the whole can. I feel like I really don't have to use that many, and I've even heard of some people switching completely over to cloth towels, which is just INSANITY to me based on how much I'd need to use them.

Anyone else have this problem? Any good ways to get better at using less?

How do I tell if people genuinely like the food I make?

I am not a chef or in a line of work that requires cooking so this is just a showerthought. 

So when you have guests or friends over and if you cook a meal for them, most of them will say they absolutely loved it out of courtesy and to not look rude. Not once in any intimate social gatherings have I come across anyone who said to the host that the food is not good. No matter how good or how bad the food is, people always say something positive.


So how do I as the person cooking that evening know if people genuinely liked the food or not? Do they have to ask for recipes? Do I judge by servings they take?

What are some of your favorite ways to spice up quick/box meals?

Sometimes a quick easy box meal just is what I want and I was curious what are some of your ways that you spice up box/quick meals.
Some examples: 

Adding burger seasoning to hamburger helper when cooking the ground beef.

Adding real cheese to box macaroni and cheese

Adding pepper flakes to beef ramen noodles

None of these examples are anything special, but taste much better than just following the box instructions.
